stem: Which entry removes the **cost** of an asset that has been sold from the asset account?

options.content: Debit disposal account; credit asset at cost account
options.rationale: Correct: the asset account is cleared of the cost of the asset sold.

options.content: Debit asset at cost account; credit disposal account
options.rationale: This is the reverse and would increase the asset.

options.content: Debit provision for depreciation; credit asset at cost account
options.rationale: The provision is cleared in a separate entry, credited to disposal.

options.content: Debit bank; credit asset at cost account
options.rationale: Proceeds are credited to the disposal account, not the asset account.

explanation: Step 1: Dr disposal, Cr asset at cost with the cost of the asset sold.

stem: How is the profit or loss on disposal of a non-current asset calculated?

options.content: Proceeds less carrying amount at the date of disposal
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: Proceeds less original cost of the asset
options.rationale: This ignores the depreciation already charged.

options.content: Carrying amount less original cost of the asset
options.rationale: Proceeds are left out.

options.content: Proceeds less the depreciation charged in the year of sale
options.rationale: Only the total accumulated depreciation is relevant, and not on its own.

explanation: Carrying amount = cost less accumulated depreciation. Proceeds above it give a profit; below it, a loss.

stem: A machine cost US\$24,000 and had accumulated depreciation of US\$15,600 when it was sold for US\$6,900. What was the result on disposal?

options.content: Loss of US\$1,500
options.rationale: Correct: carrying amount 8,400, proceeds 6,900.

options.content: Profit of US\$1,500
options.rationale: Proceeds are below the carrying amount, so it is a loss.

options.content: Loss of US\$17,100
options.rationale: This compares proceeds with cost and ignores depreciation.

options.content: Loss of US\$8,700
options.rationale: This compares proceeds with the accumulated depreciation.

explanation: Carrying amount 24,000 − 15,600 = 8,400. Proceeds 6,900 − 8,400 = loss of 1,500.

stem: Where is a profit on disposal of a non-current asset shown?

options.content: As part of revenue, increasing gross profit
options.rationale: Revenue is from the sale of goods or services in the ordinary course.

options.content: As other income in the statement of profit or loss
options.rationale: Correct: it is not trading income.

options.content: As a deduction from the cost of sales
options.rationale: Cost of sales is for goods sold.

options.content: Directly in the statement of financial position as a reserve
options.rationale: It reaches equity through the profit for the year.

explanation: A profit on disposal is other income; a loss is an expense. Neither belongs in revenue or cost of sales.
hints: Is the sale of a van part of the normal trading activity?

stem: Tendai trades in an old pump for a new one with a list price of US\$52,000. The supplier allows US\$11,500 for the old pump and Tendai pays the rest by bank transfer. At what amount is the new pump recorded in the asset account?

options.rationale: This is the cash paid only.
This is the allowance for the old pump.
The allowance is part of the price, not an addition to it.
Correct: allowance 11,500 plus cash 40,500.

explanation: Debit the asset with 11,500 (credit disposal) and 40,500 (credit bank): 52,000 in total.
hints: The new asset is recorded at its full cost.

stem: A business makes a loss on the disposal of a vehicle. What does this suggest about the depreciation charged in earlier years?

options.content: It was too high, so the carrying amount was lower than the value realised
options.rationale: That would give a profit on disposal.

options.content: It was too low, so the carrying amount was higher than the value realised
options.rationale: Correct: the loss corrects under-depreciation.

options.content: It was exactly right, so the loss was caused by the buyer
options.rationale: With correct depreciation the result would be nil.

options.content: It was not charged in the year of sale
options.rationale: The year-of-sale rule is a policy; it does not explain the loss.

explanation: Proceeds below the carrying amount mean the asset was carried at too high a value, so earlier depreciation was too low.

stem: Chipo sells a delivery truck on credit to Mr Dube. Which entry records the proceeds due from him?

options.content: Debit bank; credit disposal account
options.rationale: No cash has yet been received.

options.content: Debit disposal account; credit Mr Dube's account
options.rationale: This would record the proceeds as owed by the business.

options.content: Debit Mr Dube's account; credit asset at cost account
options.rationale: The credit for proceeds goes to the disposal account.

options.content: Debit Mr Dube's account; credit disposal account
options.rationale: Correct: the buyer owes the proceeds.

explanation: Dr buyer (a receivable), Cr disposal with the proceeds. Bank is debited when he pays.
hints: Who owes whom after a sale on credit?

stem: A sprayer was bought on 1 January 2023 for US\$38,400. Depreciation is 10% per annum on cost, straight line, on a monthly basis. It was sold on 31 March 2025. What is the accumulated depreciation to be transferred to the disposal account?

options.rationale: This leaves out the three months of 2025.
This charges a full year for 2025.
Correct: 2 years at 3,840 plus 3 months at 320.
This charges four months of 2025, one month too many.

hints: Months owned in 2025: January, February and March.

stem: In a part-exchange, the trade-in allowance given for the old asset is treated as the proceeds of the old asset.
explanation: True. Credit the disposal account with the allowance and debit the new asset account.

stem: When one van is sold, the whole balance on the provision for depreciation: vehicles account is transferred to the disposal account.
explanation: False. Only the accumulated depreciation on the van sold is transferred; the other vehicles keep theirs.
hints: Are the other vehicles still owned?

stem: Match each item with its double entry.

left.content: Part-exchange allowance received for the old asset
Accumulated depreciation on the asset sold

right.content: Debit statement of profit or loss; credit disposal
Debit disposal; credit statement of profit or loss
Debit provision for depreciation; credit disposal

explanation: A loss is a credit balancing figure in the disposal account, so the expense is debited to the statement of profit or loss; a profit is the opposite.

stem: Complete the statements about a disposal.

payload.template: Profit on disposal = proceeds − {{blank:a}}. A loss on disposal is shown as an {{blank:b}} in the statement of profit or loss.

explanation: The carrying amount is cost less accumulated depreciation; a loss is an expense.

stem: Sipho bought a milling machine on 1 January 2021 for US\$56,000. Depreciation is 10% per annum on cost, with a full year's charge in the year of purchase and none in the year of sale. He sold the machine on 15 September 2025 for US\$31,000. Calculate the loss on disposal.
explanation: Depreciation 5,600 a year for 4 years = 22,400; carrying amount 33,600. Loss 33,600 − 31,000 = 2,600. Charging 2025 as well gives a carrying amount of 28,000 and a wrong result (a profit of 3,000).
workedSolution: 1. Depreciation 5,600 a year for 4 years = 22,400; carrying amount 33,600. Loss 33,600 − 31,000 = 2,600. Charging 2025 as well gives a carrying amount of 28,000 and a wrong result (a profit of 3,000).

stem: Nyasha bought a vending machine on 1 October 2023 for US\$18,600. It is depreciated at 20% per annum on cost, straight line, on a monthly basis. She sold it on 30 November 2025 for US\$9,000. Calculate the loss on disposal.
explanation: Monthly charge 310. Months: 3 + 12 + 11 = 26, so depreciation 8,060. Carrying amount 10,540; loss 10,540 − 9,000 = 1,540. Counting 24 months gives 2,160.
workedSolution: 1. Monthly charge 310. Months: 3 + 12 + 11 = 26, so depreciation 8,060. Carrying amount 10,540; loss 10,540 − 9,000 = 1,540. Counting 24 months gives 2,160.
hints: Count the months: October to December 2023, all of 2024, January to November 2025.

stem: A new refrigerated display costs US\$38,500. The supplier allows US\$14,200 for the old display in part-exchange. How much must be paid in cash?
explanation: 38,500 − 14,200 = 24,300. The allowance covers part of the price.
workedSolution: 1. 38,500 − 14,200 = 24,300. The allowance covers part of the price.

stem: Farai bought a grinder for US\$30,000 and depreciated it at 20% per annum on the reducing balance for three full years. He then sold it for US\$17,000. Calculate the profit on disposal.
hints: Multiply by 80% each year to find the carrying amount.

stem: Name the ledger account that is used to calculate the profit or loss when a non-current asset is sold.
explanation: The disposal account brings together cost, accumulated depreciation and proceeds.

stem: Explain how a part-exchange of an old machine for a new one is recorded in the ledger.

points.description: The allowance is credited to the disposal account as the proceeds of the old machine
The new machine is debited at its full cost (allowance plus cash paid)
The cash paid is credited to bank (or the supplier's account if bought on credit)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The trade-in allowance is treated as the proceeds of the old machine, so it is credited to the disposal account. The new machine is debited at its full cost, which is the allowance plus the cash paid, and the cash element is credited to bank.

explanation: Three marks: allowance as proceeds, new asset at full cost, credit for the balance.
hints: The new asset's cost is the full price.

stem: Explain why a profit on disposal of a van is not included in revenue.

points.description: Revenue arises from the sale of goods or services in the ordinary course of business
The van is a non-current asset bought for use, not for resale
The profit is a correction of depreciation (other income) and is shown separately in the statement of profit or loss

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Revenue comes from the business's normal trading. A van is held for use, not for resale, so its sale is not trading. The profit on disposal is a correction of earlier depreciation and is shown as other income.

explanation: Distinguish trading income from other income.

stem: The owner of a tuck-shop chain sees a loss on disposal of US\$3,000 on a refrigerator and says: "We made a mistake buying that refrigerator." Evaluate this statement.

points.description: A loss means proceeds were below the carrying amount, so earlier depreciation was too low
It is an adjustment to earlier profits, not necessarily a poor purchase
The refrigerator may have earned good revenue during its life (compare total benefit with total cost)
Conclusion: the statement is not justified by the loss alone; review the depreciation rate or useful life

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The loss shows that the refrigerator was carried at more than it realised, so too little depreciation was charged in earlier years. It does not prove a bad purchase because the refrigerator may have earned good revenue. The owner should review the depreciation rate and useful life rather than judge the purchase from the loss alone.

explanation: A balanced answer separates the accounting correction from the quality of the investment.
hints: What does a loss on disposal actually correct?

stem: Chipo's hardware business in Chinhoyi owns delivery trucks. At 1 January 2025 the trucks had a total cost of US\$132,000 and accumulated depreciation of US\$61,800. Trucks are depreciated at 15% per annum on cost, with a full year's charge in the year of purchase and none in the year of sale. One truck, bought on 1 January 2021 for US\$48,000, was sold on 10 October 2025 for US\$15,000, received by bank transfer. No trucks were bought in 2025. Her year end is 31 December.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the accumulated depreciation on the truck sold.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Prepare the disposal of truck account.

points.description: Debit: trucks at cost 48,000
Credit: provision for depreciation 28,800
Credit: bank 15,000
Credit: statement of profit or loss (loss) 4,200, with totals of 48,000

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Disposal of truck account**

| Date | Details | US\$ | Date | Details | US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| 10 Oct 2025 | Motor trucks at cost | 48,000 | 10 Oct 2025 | Provision for depreciation | 28,800 |
|  |  |  | 10 Oct 2025 | Bank | 15,000 |
|  |  |  | 31 Dec 2025 | Statement of profit or loss (loss) | 4,200 |
|  |  | **48,000** |  |  | **48,000** |

parts.explanation: The loss is the credit balancing figure.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the depreciation charge on trucks for 2025.
parts.explanation: No charge on the truck sold: 15% × (132,000 − 48,000) = 12,600.
parts.workedSolution: 1. No charge on the truck sold: 15% × (132,000 − 48,000) = 12,600.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the accumulated depreciation on trucks at 31 December 2025.

explanation: This item practises a disposal for cash and the effect on the provision and the year's charge.
hints: Remove the sold truck's cost and its own depreciation from the totals.
A loss is the credit balancing figure.

stem: Thandeka runs a printing business in Gweru. On 30 June 2025 she sold a printing press that had cost US\$60,000 and had accumulated depreciation of US\$41,250 to Mr Dube for US\$16,000, payable in 60 days. On the same day she bought a new press for US\$75,000 on credit from PrintTech.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the loss on disposal of the old press.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Prepare the journal entries to record the disposal, the purchase of the new press and the transfer of the loss. Narratives are required.

points.description: Dr Disposal 60,000, Cr Printing presses at cost 60,000
Dr Provision for depreciation 41,250, Cr Disposal 41,250
Dr Mr Dube 16,000, Cr Disposal 16,000
Dr Printing presses 75,000, Cr PrintTech 75,000
Dr Statement of profit or loss 2,750, Cr Disposal 2,750
Dates and narratives

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Journal**

| Date | Details | Debit US\$ | Credit US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 30 Jun | Disposal of printing press | 60,000 |  |
|  | Printing presses at cost |  | 60,000 |
|  | *Cost of the press sold* |  |  |
| 30 Jun | Provision for depreciation: printing presses | 41,250 |  |
|  | Disposal of printing press |  | 41,250 |
|  | *Depreciation on the press sold* |  |  |
| 30 Jun | Mr Dube (other receivable) | 16,000 |  |
|  | Disposal of printing press |  | 16,000 |
|  | *Proceeds due from Mr Dube* |  |  |
| 30 Jun | Printing presses at cost | 75,000 |  |
|  | PrintTech (other payable) |  | 75,000 |
|  | *New press bought on credit* |  |  |
| 31 Dec | Statement of profit or loss | 2,750 |  |
|  | Disposal of printing press |  | 2,750 |
|  | *Loss on disposal of the press* |  |  |

parts.explanation: The sale and the purchase are both on credit, so no bank entry is made.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Where is the result on disposal shown in the statement of profit or loss?

options.content: As part of revenue
options.rationale: A loss cannot be revenue.

options.content: As part of cost of sales
options.rationale: Cost of sales is for goods sold.

options.content: As an expense
options.rationale: Correct: a loss is an expense.

options.content: It is not shown there
options.rationale: Both profits and losses on disposal are shown.

parts.explanation: A loss on disposal is an expense; a profit is other income.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State when the bank account will be affected by the sale.

points.description: When Mr Dube pays (debit bank, credit Mr Dube)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: When Mr Dube pays the US\$16,000 in 60 days.

explanation: This item practises journal entries for a disposal where both the sale and the purchase are on credit.
hints: The buyer owes the proceeds; the supplier is owed the price of the new press.
A loss is a credit balancing figure on the disposal account.
